Series::threshold_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series& Series::threshold_(double threshold_val, double value)

Mutating A Lower Region¶

threshold_() is the mutating form of threshold(). Every lane greater than threshold_val is retained; every lane less than or equal to it is replaced by value. The receiver keeps its shape, dtype, platform, and object identity, and the returned reference is the receiver itself.

Choose this form when the old values are no longer needed and mutation is compatible with the surrounding ownership and differentiation rules. Prefer the out-of-place form when the receiver is shared, reused in another branch, or is a reverse-mode leaf whose original value must remain available.

Floating and integral receivers are supported. Bool and complex receivers are rejected. Fractional thresholds are compared without truncation even for an integral receiver; the replacement itself is converted to the receiver dtype. The strict retention rule means a lane exactly on the threshold is replaced.

Reverse Mode And Mutation Safety¶

Legal in-place use records the same piecewise derivative as threshold(): retained lanes pass upstream sensitivity and replaced lanes receive zero. Mutation safety is checked before data are overwritten. An operation that would invalidate a required saved value or illegally modify a tracked leaf is rejected rather than silently corrupting the graph.

Examples¶

1. Replace lanes in the existing object¶

auto x = pluss::make_series({-1.0, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0});
x.threshold_(0.0, 7.0);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[7.0000, 7.0000, 0.5000, 1.0000]

Both -1 and the boundary value 0 are replaced.

2. Chain through the returned receiver reference¶

auto x = pluss::make_series({-1.0, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0});
auto* before = &x;
auto& returned = x.threshold_(0.0, 7.0);
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "same object=" << (&returned == before) << '\n';

Output¶

same object=true

The reference return permits deliberate fluent mutation without creating a second Series object.

3. Preserve matrix shape while mutating values¶

auto matrix = pluss::make_series({{-2.0, 0.0}, {2.0, 4.0}});
matrix.threshold_(1.0, 10.0);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, matrix);

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 10.0000 10.0000 ⎤
⎣  2.0000  4.0000 ⎦

Shape and metadata are unchanged; only qualifying lanes are overwritten.
